quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What affects your ability to stop?
questions.correctAnswerText: The condition of the road.
questions.explanation: Road conditions greatly affect how well you can stop. Poor roads are slippery and make it harder to stop safely. Always slow down on poor road conditions.

questions.question: Does drinking coffee after alcohol change your blood alcohol level?

options.text: It lowers your blood alcohol level.
It cancels the effects of alcohol.
It has no effect on your blood alcohol level.
It raises your blood alcohol level.

questions.correctAnswerText: It has no effect on your blood alcohol level.
questions.explanation: Coffee will not change your blood alcohol level. It may keep you awake, but it does not make you sober or reduce alcohol in your body.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line in the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Lanes go in opposite directions and you cannot pass.
Lanes go in opposite directions and you can pass when safe.
Lanes go in the same direction and you cannot pass.
Lanes go in the same direction and you can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes go in opposite directions and you cannot pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, what should you do?

options.text: Always have the right-of-way over vehicles in a crosswalk.
Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are coming.
Enter a crosswalk anytime because drivers must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are coming.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way, a fast-moving vehicle may not have time to stop.

questions.question: You should never drive through, around, or under railroad gates or barriers.
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Never drive through, around, or under railroad gates or barriers. It is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: If you are driving slowly and traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Pull to the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
Do not let other cars pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is dangerous. If traffic backs up behind you on a two-lane road, pull off to the right and let other vehicles pass.

questions.question: How can you avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes or turning, turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Do not rely on mirrors alone.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: You must stop immediately and back up.
You should drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Difficult driving conditions are present.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange and warn you that work is happening on or near the road. Drive carefully when you see these signs.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is coming. Watch for traffic crossing your path.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A road joins from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is ahead with a road joining from the right.

questions.question: To drive safely, you should make sure your physical condition is good. What should you do?

options.text: Stay physically fit and get regular physical exams.
Know how any medicine you take affects your driving.
Drive only within your physical limits.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Your physical condition affects how safely you can drive. Know your limits and only drive when it is safe.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: One driver should continue without stopping.
One driver should wave the others ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrives first.
questions.explanation: All drivers must stop at a four-way stop. The first driver to reach the intersection goes first. If two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line in the center of the road mean?

options.text: You can pass if it is safe.
Both lanes go in the same direction.
You can pass even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A single dashed yellow line means traffic going both directions can pass. You can only pass if you will not hit oncoming traffic.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: You must wait for police to arrive.
You must leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car, try to find the owner. If you cannot, leave a written note with your name, address, and details of the accident.

questions.question: What is the "No zone"?

options.text: Blind spots around trucks and buses.
A road where you must keep your stereo quiet.
A TV show like The Twilight Zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blind spots around trucks and buses.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on both sides, in the back, and in the front. Cars cannot be seen in these areas. These are called "No zones."

questions.question: What does this black and yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way only.
There is a detour to the right because of roadwork.
Slow down because the road turns sharply ahead.
There is a crossroad to your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down because the road turns sharply ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead has a sharp turn (in this case, to the right). Slow down before a sharp curve just like you would at an intersection.

questions.question: When the driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down to give them room to pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give them room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: When someone wants to pass you, slow down. This gives them more room to pass quickly and safely.

questions.question: What type of sign is diamond-shaped?
questions.correctAnswerText: Road hazard sign.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs are yellow warning signs. They warn you about hazards or areas where special rules apply.

questions.question: Drivers may not pass from either side of a ____ centerline.
questions.correctAnswerText: Double solid yellow
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.question: If someone drinks alcohol, what will help them get over its effects?
questions.correctAnswerText: Only time
questions.explanation: Only time will reduce the effects of alcohol.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic. You must also always yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: How should you use a freeway exit ramp?

options.text: Slow down before entering the exit ramp.
Slow down once you move onto the exit ramp.
Keep your speed the same once in the exit ramp.
Pass slower traffic in the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down once you move onto the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down until you move onto the exit ramp. Then reduce your speed.

questions.question: Is driving at night more or less dangerous than driving during the day?
questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous than day driving. It is harder to see, headlight glare can blind you, and more tired or impaired drivers are on the road.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk or on overcast days. Use low beams when within 1,000 feet of an oncoming vehicle or within 500 feet of a vehicle ahead of you. Always use low beams in bad weather.

questions.question: A driver entering a public road from a driveway or private road:

options.text: Must yield to drivers already on the public road.
Can force their way into traffic.
Can assume other drivers will make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: If you enter traffic from a driveway or private road, you must yield to drivers already on the public road. Merge safely when it is possible to do so.
